plan.title: hardening(hooks): lock operator-override eligibility across host entry points

narratives.Description: hardening(hooks): lock operator-override eligibility across host entry points
narratives.Overview:
## Problem statement
Make the existing operator-disable contract an explicit conformance boundary for generated host entry points and the policy detector. Cover both eligibility and indeterminate-state handling without changing the supported operator workflow.

## Required behavior
- An operator-disable override is eligible only at the project root, for a non-symlink regular file, after a successful repository-tracking check establishes that it is untracked. A tracked entry is not eligible. Other filesystem objects and unresolved metadata are not eligible.
- Distinguish a successful untracked result from an inspection/probe failure. Missing tooling, process failures, abnormal termination, unreadable state, and filesystem inspection errors must never grant the override. Do not cache an indeterminate result as a successful untracked result.
- When no eligible override exists, retain normal hook enforcement and propagate the runtime decision. If safe evaluation or runtime dispatch is unavailable, retain the host's fail-closed response and recovery guidance; never substitute an unconditional allow.
- Preserve the existing valid operator workflow: a positively validated local override remains usable before the project runtime is installed. Keep the generated entry point Node-built-ins-only until its entry checks complete; do not introduce a dependency on the missing runtime to evaluate the override.
- Keep the policy detector and generated host entry points consistent on these eligibility/error semantics. Preserve host-specific deny/error protocols, project-root binding, and installation-recovery behavior.

## Implementation scope
Primary implementation and tests:
- `packages/core/src/init-deposit/host-hook-outer.ts`
- `packages/core/src/init-deposit/host-hook-outer.test.ts`
- `packages/core/src/policy/deft-directive-disable.ts`
- `packages/core/src/policy/deft-directive-disable.test.ts`

Use existing helpers where compatible with the standalone entry-point constraint, otherwise enforce parity through shared conformance cases. Refresh any repository-owned generated entry-point fixtures/deposits only through the existing generation path, with content-derived filenames/hashes. Do not hand-edit hashes or modify consumer checkouts.

## Acceptance criteria and refusal tests
1. **Eligibility matrix:** table-driven policy and generated-entry-point tests cover valid local regular-file state, tracked state, absent state, ineligible filesystem-kind fixtures, and indeterminate inspection/tracking state. Only a positively validated eligible state selects the operator override.
2. **Enforcement retained:** for every ineligible state, use a deterministic test runtime whose policy response is deny. The generated entry point must reach normal enforcement and preserve that refusal; an empty successful process result is not a sufficient assertion. With the test runtime unavailable, assert the existing host-specific fail-closed response instead.
3. **Unknown is not permission:** inject filesystem inspection errors and Git launch/probe errors, abnormal termination, and unsuccessful probe outcomes. Assert that none selects the override. Distinguish these cases from a successful probe with no tracked entry; test both cached and fresh policy-detector paths.
4. **Valid compatibility control:** a positively validated local regular-file override retains the documented early-disable behavior even without the project runtime. Make the fixture's repository-tracking result explicit and deterministic; do not rely on failure outside a repository as evidence of being untracked.
5. **Host conformance:** exercise generated entry-point behavior for Grok, Claude, Cursor, and Codex using their existing event/protocol fixtures. Assert the actual host refusal output/status for negative cases, not merely a source-string match or exit status shared by allow and deny.
6. **Generation and regression:** generated content hashes and registered commands remain consistent. Run the two focused suites above and affected existing host-deposit/protocol checks. No new skips, platform-privilege dependencies, or weakened assertions. Document the focused test results in the PR.

## Out of scope
No new features, new override mechanism, broader write-authorization catalog, host-root policy changes, timeout redesign, dependency/bootstrap redesign, safety-check disabling, or manual edits to consumer deposits. Preserve the valid missing-runtime workflow tracked by #5809; this issue does not absorb or close that work.

## Tracking
Refs #6034

The implementation PR must use `Refs #6034`, never an auto-closing reference to #6034. That issue remains open for its other items. Completion here is limited to the control and tests above, not disposition of the parent issue.

Filed for @MScottAdams

items.title: Introduce three-way eligibility distinguishing positively validated eligible from ineligible and indeterminate; only eligible selects operator override
Require successfully completed git ls-files listing with usable captured output; launch failure nonzero or unavailable output is indeterminate
Do not cache indeterminate probe results as untracked success; later successful tracked probe must re-probe and remain inactive
Outer uses lstat regular-file parity with policy; table-driven tests cover adapters and generated host fixtures for four hosts
Positively validated eligible override remains usable before project runtime is installed Node-built-ins-only
Extend policy and host-hook-outer tests for eligibility matrix cache transitions and host refusal survival
